title: Tuesday, September 8, 2026

headline.title: The weekend did more than the jobs print did. The US struck Iranian tankers, Iran struck back, Iranian-aligned forces hit Saudi Aramco's Jazan refinery, and Tehran says an Oman deal for a “safe route” through Hormuz is days away. WTI is pressing $94 and Brent is knocking on $100 — a six-week high, and crude is up more than 30% since late February. Energy is the whole Failed 2D board this morning: USO +2.49%, SHEL +1.88%, OXY +1.81%, MPC +1.70%, XOM +1.29%, XLE +1.08%.
headline.summary: And ORCL is the single name doing the most work. It gaps +5.52% to 167.55, above Friday's 159.70 high and above every level of the prior two sessions, with the backlog reported at $638B, up 363% year-over-year and the print landing Thursday after the close. Underneath, the memory trade refuses to cool — MU +1.06% through $1,027, SNDK +0.80% after closing Friday at its high — on a Friday board where SNDK pulled $5.1B and MU $5.0B of cumulative dark-pool size, over $10B across the two names. The index itself is the coil: SPY, IWM and META all printed Inside (1) on Friday, and SPY's premarket 768.28 is already below Friday's 769.00 low.

overview: Two tracks, and they are pulling opposite ways. Energy and semis are green; the index is not. SPY premarket 768.28 sits below Friday's 769.00 low, which breaks the inside bar down before the bell, while QQQ +0.10% holds because ORCL, TSM, MU, SNDK and AVGO are all bid. Friday's macro is still the frame: payrolls 162k against ~55k, unemployment 4.1%, wages +0.3%, and June and July revised up a combined 55k after a long run of downgrades. The 10-year is at ~4.77% with 2- and 5-year yields at 52-week highs, and the hike is priced somewhere between a coin flip and ~60%. What the tape did with that on Friday is the thing to keep in view: the Dow fell 272 points and the Russell closed green, so it was not a broad de-risking. Today is quiet by design — NFIB small-business optimism this morning, July consumer credit at 2:00pm CT, and the Fed is in its pre-meeting quiet period, so there are no speakers between here and PPI Thursday and CPI Friday. Canada's retaliatory tariffs on $20B of US goods take effect today.

setups: Friday was a 2 Up — H 159.70 over Thursday's 156.77, L 156.71 above Thursday's 146.92 — closing 158.78 near the top of it. Premarket 167.55 is nearly eight dollars above that high and above every level of the prior two sessions. The number behind it: a backlog reported at $638B, up 363% year-over-year, with the print landing Thursday after the close. Over 159.70 is the structure and it is already well through. The tension is that the whole move is happening two sessions before the event that justifies it — this is a gap into a catalyst, not out of one, which is the shape MRVL had on 8/27 before it gave the entire thing back into its own print.

Friday was a 2 Down — L 63.375 under Thursday's 64.5825, H 64.33 under Thursday's 65.52 — closing 64.06 back above the low. Premarket 64.75 clears Friday's 64.33 high, which completes the failed 2 Down. This is the cleanest thematic on the board because it is not one name: USO +2.49%, SHEL +1.88% (Outside 3 resolving up, printing at an all-time high), OXY +1.81%, MPC +1.70%, XOM +1.29% — and MPC, XOM and OXY are each completing their own failed 2 Downs off Friday's lows. Over 64.33 is the trigger. The risk is explicit and dated: Tehran says the Oman “safe route” deal is days away, and that headline unwinds this.

Friday was a 2 Up entirely above Thursday — H 429.82 / L 419.42, closing 428.91 near the high. Premarket 436.05 is through it. What makes this more than a continuation is the stacking: Friday's largest options block on either board was $44.6M of TSM $380C 11/20, deep in the money; this morning's largest dark-pool print is TSM at $50.0M on the ask; and the monthly sales update lands Thursday with a dividend the week after. Deep ITM calls that far out often read as synthetic stock rather than a directional bet, so treat it as size and structure, not intent. Over 429.82 continues it.

darkpool.note: Third straight session the board leaned ask, and Friday was emphatic. The largest print on the entire tape was SPY $1.3B (ask, AH) with IVV $1.3B (ask) right behind it, and the ex-ETF list runs ask nearly top to bottom — GOOGL $500M bid was the lone bid in the top ten. On cumulative flow the index complex leads the whole board at IVV $5.6B ask and SPY $5.4B ask, which means broad-index money has now leaned ask into and out of the hot jobs print, with the inflation pair dead ahead. The one to sit with is memory: SNDK pulled $5.1B cumulative and MU $5.0B — the two largest single-name lines on the board, over $10B combined — and both were mixed, not bid, on the very session they ripped 7% and 5%. Size on both sides of a name that is going straight up is a different signal from one-way accumulation. And NVDA's $4.8B flipped to ask after a week of bid prints at the top.

tts.text: The levels that matter today. Oracle, one fifty nine seventy, Friday's high, already cleared by eight dollars. X L E, sixty four thirty three, Friday's high, cleared premarket. Taiwan Semi, four twenty nine eighty two. Micron, one thousand seventeen seventy seven, Friday's high. Broadcom, three sixty sixty, where it failed on Friday.
